text:
Three elements X, Y and Z are in the $3^{rd}$ period
of the periodic table. The oxides of X, Y and Z,
respectively, are basic, amphoteric and acidic.
The correct order of the atomic numbers of X,
Y and Z is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When we are moving from left to right in a
periodic table along with atomic number of atom acidic character of oxides also increases.

$\therefore$ atomic number : X < Y < Z

then acidic character : X < Y < Z

text:
Simplified absorption spectra of three
complexes ((i), (ii) and (iii)) of $M^{n+}$ ion are
provided below; their $λ_{\max }$ values are marked
as A, B and C respectively. The correct match
between the complexes and their $λ_{\max }$ values is

[IMG]


(i) [M(NCS$)_{6}$]$^{(–6 + n)}$

(ii) [$MF_{6}$]$^{(–6 + n)}$

(iii) [$M(NH_{3})_{6}$]$^{n+}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The energy of the absorbed light equals the crystal field splitting, $\Delta _{o}=\dfrac{hc}{λ_{\max }}$, so a stronger field ligand gives a shorter $λ_{\max }$.

In the spectrochemical series N-bonded thiocyanate ($\mathrm{NCS}{}^{-}$) lies above $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and hence above $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ (only S-bonded $\mathrm{SCN}{}^{-}$ lies below $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$), and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is stronger still: $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}<\mathrm{NCS}{}^{-}<\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$.

So $λ_{\max }$ increases in the order (iii) $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{n+}$ < (i) $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{NCS})_{6}]^{(n-6)}$ < (ii) $[\mathrm{MF}_{6}]^{(n-6)}$.

In the spectra $λ_{\max }$ increases in the order A < B < C, so A = (iii), B = (i) and C = (ii).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
The results given in the below table were
obtained during kinetic studies of the following
reaction

2A + B $\to$ C + D

[IMG]


X and Y in the given table are respectively :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Rate $=k[\mathrm{A}]^{a}[\mathrm{B}]^{b}$.

Experiments I and III: $[\mathrm{B}]$ is fixed and $[\mathrm{A}]$ doubles, while the rate changes from $6.00\times 10^{-3}$ to $1.20\times 10^{-2}$, i.e. doubles, so $a=1$.

Experiments I and II: $[\mathrm{A}]$ is fixed and $[\mathrm{B}]$ doubles, while the rate changes from $6.00\times 10^{-3}$ to $2.40\times 10^{-2}$, i.e. becomes 4 times, so $b=2$.

From experiment I:

$k=\dfrac{6.00\times 10^{-3}}{(0.1)(0.1)^{2}}=6\text{L}^{2}\text{mol}^{-2}\text{\min }^{-1}$

Experiment IV:

$7.20\times 10^{-2}=6\times X\times (0.2)^{2}\Rightarrow X=\dfrac{7.20\times 10^{-2}}{0.24}=0.3$

Experiment V:

$2.88\times 10^{-1}=6\times 0.3\times Y^{2}\Rightarrow Y^{2}=\dfrac{0.288}{1.8}=0.16\Rightarrow Y=0.4$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
The oxidation states of transition metal atoms
in $K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}$, KMnO$_{4}$ and $K_{2}$FeO$_{4}$, respectively,
are x, y and z. The sum of x, y and z is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}$

Let oxidation state of Ce

2(+1) + 2x + 7(–2) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ x = +6

In $K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}$, Transition metal (Cr) present in +6 oxidation state.

KMnO$_{4}$

(+1) + y + 4(–2) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ x = +7

In KMnO$_{4}$, transition metal (Mn) present in +7
oxidation state.

$K_{2}$FeO$_{4}$

2(+1) + z + 4(–2) = 0

$\Rightarrow$x = +6

In $K_{2}$FeO$_{4}$, transition metal (Fe) present in +6
oxidation state.

$\therefore$ x + y + z = 6 + 7 + 6 = 19

text:
The heat of combustion of ethanol into carbon
dioxide and water is – 327 kcal at constant
pressure. The heat evolved (in cal) at constant
volume and $27^{o}C ($if all gases behave ideally) is
(R = 2 cal mol$^{–1} K^{–1}) ________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{2}H_{5}OH (l) + 3O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $2CO_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}O(l)$

$\Delta$H = –327 kcal; $\Deltan_{g} = – 1$

$\Delta$H = $\Delta$U + $\Deltan_{g}RT$

$\Rightarrow$ $\DeltaU =  – 327 + 2 × 10^{–3} × 300$

= – 326.4 kcal

= – 326400 cal

$\therefore$ Heat evolved = 326400 cal.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot

text:
The ratio of the mass percentages of ‘C & H’
and ‘C & O’ of a saturated acyclic organic
compound ‘X’ are 4 : 1 and 3 : 4 respectively.
Then, the moles of oxygen gas required for
complete combustion of two moles of organic
compound ‘X’ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the organic compound X is $= C_{x}H_{y}O_{z}$

Here moles of C = x, moles of H = y, moles of O = z

Given, $\frac{W_{C}}{W_{H}}=\frac{4}{1}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{\frac{WC}{12}}{\frac{WH}{1}}$ = $\frac{4}{1}\times \frac{1}{12}$ = $\frac{1}{3}$

Also Given, $\frac{W_{C}}{W_{O}}=\frac{3}{4}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x}{z}=\frac{\frac{WC}{12}}{\frac{WO}{16}}$ = $\frac{3}{4}\times \frac{16}{12}$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ x = z

$\therefore$ Empirical formula $= C_{x}H_{3x}O_{x} = CH_{3}O$

As compound is saturated acyclic organic
 compound, so molecular formula $= C_{2}H_{6}O_{2}$

$C_{2}H_{6}O_{2} +$ $\frac{5}{2}O_{2}$ $\to$ $2CO_{2} + 3H_{2}O$

For 1 mole of $C_{2}H_{6}O_{2}$ number of moles of $O_{2}$ required = $\frac{5}{2}$

$\therefore$ For 2 mole of $C_{2}H_{6}O_{2}$ number of moles 
of $O_{2}$ required = $\frac{5}{2}$ $\times$ 2 = 5
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 2nd September Evening Slot
